us.title: Which magnetic wireless speed is my iPhone? Wireless charging speeds compared
us.description: Macworld Not having to find the right cable or carry one around with you makes wireless charging a convenient way of charging your mobile devices—iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods and many third-party gadgets. There are multiple wireless charging standards and technologies. Here we will explain the major ones—Qi, MagSafe, Qi2 and the latest Qi2 25W (aka Qi2.2). Knowing which is which will help you to make your charging life more efficient. Here we look at Qi2 vs MagSafe and Qi2 25W vs Qi2 and Apple’s updated 2024 version of MagSafe. Which is best for your model of iPhone? It’s a little more nuanced, but in general, iPhones 16, 17 and 18 (and the iPhone Duo) should now charge wirelessly at up to 25W with supporting certified Qi 2.2 chargers. Older iPhones are limited to the 15W maximum if they support certified Apple MagSafe or Qi2. Chargers that are merely “MagSafe Compatible” are usually limited to 7.5W wireless charging. Note that the iPhone Air is limited to 20W wireless, the 16e to 7.5W and 17e to 15W. iPhone wireless charging speeds in brief: iPhone 8-11 series and 16e: Qi 7.5W. 0-50% in around 90 minutes. iPhone 12-15 series and 17e: MagSafe 15W and Qi2 15W. 0-50% in around 45 minutes. iPhone Air: 20W Qi2. 0-50% in around 40 minutes. iPhone 16 and 16 Pro: MagSafe 22W and Qi2.2 22W. 0-50% in around 35 minutes. iPhone 16 Plus, 17, 17/18 Pro, 16/17/18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo: MagSafe 25W and Qi2.2 25W. 0-50% in around 30 minutes. Don’t worry too much about the difference between 22W and 25W—the charging time difference will be marginal given environmental conditions such as room temperature will also make an impact. Wireless charging uses electromagnetic induction to power your devices. The charging pad and your phone both include copper wire coils. Plug the pad into a power source and the charger’s coil generates a magnetic field. When you place your phone onto the charging pad, the phone’s coil converts that magnetic field into an electric current, thus charging the phone. Apple pioneered improved magnetic connection between charger and phone with MagSafe, and it’s mainly the tighter magnetic fit that drives faster and faster wireless charging. What is Qi2? Qi2—supported by the iPhone 12 and up—speeds up wireless charging from 7.5W to 15W and makes chargers cheaper as well as more efficient. It is very like MagSafe, which is unsurprising as Apple allowed the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) to use MagSafe as the basis of Qi2. In short, Qi2 brings the magnetic benefits of MagSafe, but also make third-party iPhone chargers faster and potentially cheaper. Manufacturers are more likely to create new products when the market is larger (iPhone and Android) and costs should come down, too. Apple’s latest version of its iPhone MagSafe Charger can wirelessly charge the iPhone 16 series at 22-25W. Older iPhones can use this charger but at a 15W maximum as before. Qi2 took its time catching up, but it has now: keep reading. We have tested Qi2 chargers vs chargers certified as MagSafe by Apple, and can confirm that 15W Qi2 charges supporting devices at an equivalent speed to 15W MagSafe, and much faster than merely MagSafe-compatible 7.5W chargers. More details of our wireless charging speed tests below. Belkin What is Qi2.2 25W? The latest Qi2 25W standard (officially Qi 2.2) matches Apple’s 25W wireless charging speed. We have tested many 25W chargers, including the Belkin 25W UltraCharge Pro 3-in-1 Magnetic Charging Dock, Ugreen MagFlow Power Bank, 25W Baseus PicoGo AM52 Power Bank and ESR’s 25W CryoBoost 3-in-1 Charging Station among others. Samsung waited until its Galaxy S26 Ultra to jump on the fast magnetic wireless charging bandwagon with Qi2 25W, and Google was first out of the Android blocks with Qi2 25W compatibility with its Pixel 10 Pro XL. The lesser Google Pixel 10 Pro is pegged back at 15W Qi2. Google calls its version of Qi2 “PixelSnap”. First, let’s look at the original Qi, which all iPhones post iPhone 8 support. Foundry Qi is a Chinese word that means “energy flow”. Pronounced “chee”, Qi is the basic and most popular wireless charging standard, launched in 2008 but not seen on an iPhone until 2017’s iPhone 8. Note that plain Qi2 has little magnetic connection between phone and charger so is less efficient at transferring power as more is wasted depending on the placement of the phone on the charger. Better magnetic attachment and therefore faster charging arrived with MagSafe and Qi2. Apple continues to support the Qi wireless charging standard with its most recent iPhones—and the iPhone 12 and later models are compatible with Qi2, more on which later. This means that iPhones from the iPhone 8 onwards can be placed on a Qi-compatible charger to start charging without a cable. (Of course, the Qi charging pad or stand itself has to be connected via a cable to a power charger.) While wireless charging means less wear and tear to your devices, it is not as efficient as charging via a cable (wired charging) as some of the energy is lost between the charging pad and the device placed on it. Qi users will know that you have to ensure your device is placed in exactly the right alignment for fast wireless charging to take place. Place the iPhone on the pad incorrectly and you end up either charging much more slowly or not at all. Many of us have dropped a phone on a Qi charger only to find out later that it wasn’t in the right place and so annoyingly never started charging—a problem largely solved by Apple’s MagSafe. While Qi’s maximum wireless charge is 15W, Apple’s iPhone supports only 7.5W via Qi. Which iPhones use Qi? Qi charging is built into the iPhone 8, X, XR, XS, SE, 11, 12, 13, and 14 families. The iPhone 15/16/17/18 and Air/Duo work with Qi but are rated as Qi2; see later. The outlier is the curious iPhone 16e that goes all the way back to plain old Qi; the 17e is fine. Apple’s magnetic MagSafe iPhones contain a ring of magnets built around its Qi charging coil. As a result, you can magnetically clamp charging accessories onto the iPhone. In fact, you can magnetically attach non-charging accessories, such as wallets and mounts, too. MagSafe—from 2020’s iPhone 12 on—makes missing the charging pad’s coils much less likely with its ring of magnets quickly finding the charging alignment sweet spot—on a compatible charger—so you will always connect and less energy is wasted. Magnetic Power Profile (MPP) technology uses magnets to perfectly align the coils of the wireless charging transmitter and receiver before transferring power. iPhones can work with wireless chargers that are either MagSafe certified by Apple (“made for MagSafe”) or are compatible with MagSafe—plus less sophisticated Qi chargers. Certified MagSafe chargers can supply up to 25W to the iPhone, while merely MagSafe compatible chargers are limited to 7.5W, but compatible chargers are usually cheaper. That 25W charging speed is currently limited to the iPhone 16 and 17 ranges and Apple’s own MagSafe Charger. iPhones 12/13/14/15 max out at 15W using MagSafe. The iPhone Air won’t charge faster than 20W wirelessly. In fact, the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro are pegged back at 22W, while the larger 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max support the while 25W. The 16e is out of the picture at just 7.5W and the 17e makes it to 15W. (Note that the iPhone 12 mini only charges at 12W with MagSafe.) We have tested the best MagSafe chargers for iPhones and the best MagSafe power banks for iPhones. This reviews roundup now also includes 15W Qi2 and 25W Qi2.2 chargers as they arrive to market. Some thicker cases get in the way of MagSafe wireless charging so make sure your iPhone’s case is MagSafe compatible—see our roundup of the best iPhone 15 Cases, best iPhone 16 cases, best iPhone 17 cases and best iPhone 18 cases. Wireless charging is great, but it’s not as fast as wired charging. For truly fast iPhone charging, use a cable connected to at least a 20W USB-C charger. For the iPhone 15 and later that means a USB-C to USB-C cable; for older iPhones you’ll need a USB-C to Lightning cable. A USB-A to Lightning cable won’t offer iPhone fast charging. Click here for more iPhone fast-charging tips. Somewhat confusingly, MagSafe is also the name for Apple’s wired-charging standard for its MacBooks—connecting the charging cable to the MacBook’s MagSafe port via magnets, meaning it is not only easy to connect but, if accidentally disconnected, it pops out rather than dragging your laptop to the floor. This version of MagSafe is magnetic and safe and has a charging connection for MacBooks but is not wireless. We explain the difference between MagSafe on Mac and MagSafe on iPhones in our Complete guide to Apple MagSafe: What is MagSafe? Which iPhones use MagSafe? MagSafe wireless charging is built into the iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18 families, with the exception of the 16e. It’s also supported by the iPhone Air and iPhone Duo. Qi2 (“chee too”) is the latest version of the Qi “energy flow” wireless charging standard, and it’s supported by all iPhones from the iPhone 12. Famed for its “Not Invented Here” strategy, Apple can be quite precious about adopting other technical standards. It has a long history of rejecting any idea that didn’t originate within Apple itself. However, thankfully Apple has cooperated with the creation of Qi2 to the extent that in effect it gave the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) MagSafe to use as the basis for Qi2’s Magnetic Power Profile that defines how the new generation Qi works. Apple is a WPC “steering member” and chair of the board of directors. So what is Qi2 and why is it so great? Think of Qi2 as not just MagSafe for Android, but MagSafe benefits for all compatible wireless charging products. Qi2 means chargers won’t have to be certified by Apple to support 15W charging. They should, however, meet the technical demands of the WPC. In short, a Qi2 charger will deliver twice as fast charging as “MagSafe-compatible” chargers. As MagSafe certification costs manufacturers a fee to Apple, removing this should result in cheaper chargers that match Apple-certified chargers in terms of speed. Which iPhones use Qi2? Qi2 wireless charging works with all iPhones 12. and onwards, except the 16e. Simon Jary / Foundry Qi2 25W is the latest version of the Qi “energy flow” wireless charging standard. Its technical name is Qi2.2. It started rolling out in wireless charging products from the mid-2025 and is now seen in many new wireless charging products. So what is Qi2 25W and why is it so great? Qi2 25W means chargers can support up to 25W wireless charging. They have to meet the technical demands of the WPC. In short, a Qi2 25W charger will deliver 10W more power than Qi2 and 3.3 times as fast charging as MagSafe-compatible chargers. The use of a Magnetic Power Profile (MPP) provides better alignment but also reduces magnetic field leakage caused by misalignment. This minimizes the build-up of heat and ensures optimal charging efficiency. A ±0.5mm magnetic alignment precision improves charging efficiency by “up to 40%”, according to manufacturer Baseus. Qi2 25W products also feature next-generation thermal regulation with stricter 40°C surface limits and enhanced coil layouts. This ensures that less energy is wasted and provides 15% better charging efficiency—even in motion or with slight misalignment. Which iPhones use Qi2 25W? Qi2 25W wireless charging will work with the iPhone 16 family and later (except the 16e and 17e). The iPhone Air supports Qi2 25W but only up to 20W, which is likely caused by the super-thin phone’s thermal management. The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro can make it to only 22W according to Apple. The iPhone Duo does support 25W Qi2.2. For Qi2 25W to work at full 25W supporting iPhones must have installed at least iOS 26 or later. First, MagSafe, Qi2 and Qi2 25W are all better than plain Qi. Owing in large part to their magnetic connection, they are more efficient and definitely offer faster wireless charging than Qi. For all extents and purposes, Qi2 looks pretty identical to MagSafe so iPhone 12/13/14/15 users can choose between MagSafe or Qi2 without fear. iPhone 16/17/18/Air/Duo owners, however, should look to MagSafe or Qi2 25W, as Apple’s own MagSafe Charger and soon Qi2 25W chargers can reach charging speeds of up to 25W when paired with the latest range of iPhones. All should clamp chargers magnetically to the iPhone in the same way and allow for between 15W and 25W wireless charging. Although technically very similar, Apple is likely to still require MagSafe certification for non-Qi2 products to reach 15W wireless charging. Both the charger and the device must be certified for Qi2 for it to work at 15W, in the same way as MagSafe. However, it is likely that future MagSafe-certified products will also be certified for Qi2, and post iOS 17.2 all iPhones (except 16e) will work natively with Qi2 and Qi2.2 chargers. For consumers it’s a win-win as Qi2 and Qi2 25W means faster wireless charging will be brought to more devices and people. For product marketers it may be a bit of a labelling nightmare until all the chargeable devices catch up with the technology: expect MagSafe Compatible (7.5W), MagSafe (15W or 25W), Qi2 15W (15W) and Qi2 25W or Qi2.2 (25W). Is Qi2 as fast at wireless charging as MagSafe? As the Wireless Power Consortium used Apple technology to build the Qi2 specification, it is true that Qi2 matches MagSafe for speed. Both can charge at up to 15W and use the largely same magnetic attachment tech. Note the 25W charging potential of the Apple MagSafe Charger and iPhone 16/17, plus the same charging speed from Qi2 25W. The first Qi2 charger we tested and reviewed at Macworld was the Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station. We tested its Qi2 wireless charging speed by charging an iPhone 15 Pro all the way to a 100% full charge, and taking timings at 30%, 50% and 80%. We did the same using a Apple’s own MagSafe Charger and also via a straight wired USB-C connection. The fastest way to charge an iPhone is via a wired connection: USB-C to Lightning for iPhones older than the iPhone 15, and USB-C to USB-C for the iPhone 15 and later. The average wired-charging time in our tests was 25 minutes to 50%, 55 minutes to 80% and 70 minutes to 100%. Our wireless charging tests for officially Apple-certified MagSafe chargers (using Apple’s own Wireless Charger) and for Qi2 magnetic wireless charging (using the Anker MagGo) had remarkably similar timings. There was some variance either way but also small differences using the same charger so we are confident that using these two magentic wireless charging technologies came up with the same basic results on average: 45 minutes to 50%, 90 minutes to 80% and 115 minutes to 100%. In summary, then, MagSafe and Qi2 charging at 15W results in the same times and so can be considered equal—except for the 25W MagSafe potential of the iPhone 16/17–and the same from Qi2 25W now it is released. And, again as expected, merely MagSafe-compatible chargers took twice as long as the 15W chargers: 45 minutes to 30%, and 90 minutes to 50%. Our tests demonstate that Qi2 25W will charges an iPhone 16 Pro from 0–50% in just over 30 minutes—manufacturers often claim 25 minutes but that is under clinical conditions. In Macworld’s real-world tests 32-34 minutes is the average. In comparison, a Qi2 15W charger generally takes about 45 minutes to reach the same level—this would work out as the 25W option being around 45% faster than the 15W chargers. Wireless charging depends on many factors, such as device settings, usage during charging, and ambient temperature. Don’t concern yourself greatly about the 22W limit of the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro. The 3% difference between that and 25W is marginal. Why does phone charging speed slow down as the battery gets fuller? Batteries charge slower the fuller they get, especially in the last 10–20% of charging. The fuller the battery is, the slower it absorbs energy. To start with, a Lithium-Ion battery accepts whatever current it can, but as the battery gets closer to being full it accepts less current, and so the power being transferred tapers off. Imagine you were filling up a glass with water. You can start with the faucet or tap at full blast, but as the glass gets fuller, you have to slow the flow down to avoid the water spilling over, until eventually just a trickle of water goes in as you try to get it right up to the brim. If the battery didn’t charge this way and instead filled up at full blast till reaching 100%, it would get very hot and you’d risk damaging it to the point it might explode! Slowing down the charge when the battery is getting closer to full also increases the number of charge cycles a battery can go through before it permanently loses capacity. Taking advantage of this, if you need to charge quickly, stop at 80%, use the device for a while and then top back up to 80% before the charging speed starts to slow. Ugreen

es.title: Dani Senabre y la derrota del Barcelona ante el PSG: "Es el único equipo de Europa al que yo me siento inferior"
es.description: La derrota del FC Barcelona ante el París Saint-Germain por 4-2 en la Champions League ha supuesto un duro golpe para el equipo azulgrana, que concedió su primera derrota de la temporada. Para Dani Senabre, el partido era más importante de lo que parecía, ya que servía para medir el nivel real del equipo frente a los grandes de Europa. "Para mí el partido de hoy era más importante de lo que la gente decía para situarme. Yo quiero saber dónde estoy", ha afirmado en El Partidazo de COPE, dejando claro que el resultado ha confirmado sus sospechas. Según su análisis, la superioridad del equipo parisino ha sido evidente y demuestra que todavía hay una brecha importante entre el Barça y la élite europea. "Había un escalón entre el París Saint Germain y el Barça y yo quería saber si seguía estando, y el partido de hoy me cuenta muy a las claras que sigue existiendo", ha explicado. Dani Senabre ha ido más allá y ha calificado al conjunto francés como el rival más formidable del continente en la actualidad. "El París Saint Germain es el mejor equipo del mundo, no pasa nada por reconocerlo", ha asegurado de forma rotunda. Esta sensación de inferioridad es algo que, según el periodista, solo se produce frente al equipo dirigido por Luis Enrique. "Creo que es el único equipo de Europa al que yo me siento inferior, o que creo que el Barça se puede sentir inferior", ha confesado, para después admitir que, lógicamente, no le ha "gustado lo que ha pasado hoy". A pesar de la contundencia de su análisis, Senabre ha querido desvincular esta derrota del próximo Clásico contra el Real Madrid. El comunicador ha insistido en separar ambos partidos, pidiendo que no se haga una lectura equivocada. "Hoy no ha jugado el Madrid, lo digo porque ya me veo que va a parecer que hoy ha jugado el Madrid", ha recalcado. En este sentido, ha descartado que el resultado de Champions pueda tener un efecto negativo de cara al enfrentamiento con su máximo rival. "Nos equivocamos si leemos el partido de hoy en clave clásico, para mí no afecta al 'Clásico'", ha sentenciado, zanjando cualquier especulación al respecto al añadir que "no tiene nada que ver" con que "el Madrid nos va a meter 5".

mx.title: O2 explica qué hará si tu router está afectado por la vulnerabilidad: “Contactaremos contigo inmediatamente”
mx.description: O2 ha concretado en X cómo va a gestionar la vulnerabilidad de los chips WiFi de Broadcom que afecta a algunos de sus routers. La operadora asegura que está comprobando si existe afectación en sus equipos. En caso afirmativo, contactará con los clientes cuyo router esté afectado para informarles de inmediato y proponer una solución. Te contamos todos los detalles. La respuesta llega días después del descubrimiento de un fallo de seguridad en el software WiFi de Broadcom, presente en routers de generaciones antiguas utilizados por operadoras de distintos países. En España, el listado de equipos afectados incluye modelos empleados por Movistar, Orange, Jazztel, MásMóvil y la propia O2. Con ese escenario, la incógnita para los clientes era qué haría su operadora, y O2 ha sido una de las primeras en concretar su plan por escrito. Su equipo de redes sociales ha confirmado el protocolo en su cuenta de X, donde ha ofrecido una actualización de la situación. La respuesta, como siempre, está al nivel de la firma, que siempre se esfuerza en ofrecer la mejor experiencia de usuario. Cómo lo está gestionando O2 Desde O2 han respondido a un cliente que se ha puesto en contacto con la firma para obtener más información sobre esta cuestión. O2 ha querido despejar cualquier duda, confirmando que está comprobando si existe afectación en sus equipos, un proceso que depende también de la evolución del análisis del fallo. O2 España @o2es @alizze1976 Hola, en estos momento estamos comprobando si existe afectación a nuestros equipos. Si detectamos vulnerabilidad en tu router contactaremos contigo para inmediatamente para informarte e indicarte la resolución correspondiente. Si deseas cambiarlo puedes solicitarlo con un coste 20 de octubre, 2026 • 21:49 4 0 Según ha argumentado, si O2 detecta la vulnerabilidad en el router de un cliente, contactará con él inmediatamente para informarle y para indicarle la resolución correspondiente. El aviso no depende, por tanto, de que el usuario conozca la noticia, sino que será la propia operadora la que comunique la solución de manera proactiva. Es decir, como clientes no tendremos que hacer nada. Una vez finalice la investigación, nos proporcionará toda la información que necesitamos. Pero, ¿y si no quieres esperar al final de la investigación? En este caso, también ofrece una alternativa. El cliente puede solicitar el cambio de router por un coste de 60 euros, en modalidad autoinstalable, de modo que la sustitución no requiere cita técnica ni desplazamiento de un instalador. Si no quieres esperar, es tan fácil como ponerte en contacto con la compañía y te ayudarán a encontrar una solución. El problema no es del operador Pese a que O2 va a responder por este fallo, el origen del problema es ajeno a las compañías. La vulnerabilidad reside en el software WiFi desarrollado por Broadcom, y el componente señalado es su monitor de WPS, que permanece activo en el chip incluso cuando el usuario desactiva el WPS desde la configuración.

sg.title: Xinhua Silk Road: National Robot Test and Assessment Center (Headquarters) establishes branch in Jinan Start-up Area
sg.description: BEIJING, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Yellow River Basin Center of the National Robot Test and Assessment Center (Headquarters) was officially inaugurated in Jinan Start-up Area for Growth Drivers Transformation in Shandong Province on October 16, addressing gaps in public services for the robotics industry across the region. The National Robot Test and Assessment Center is a nationally authorized testing and certification institution in China's robotics sector, serving as a key pillar of the country's robot testing and certification system. The newly-established Yellow River Basin Center, serving Shandong and the region across the Yellow River Basin, will establish an integrated platform that combines innovation and R&D, pilot-scale testing and smart manufacturing, data collection and training, data services, testing and certification, and industrial development for complete robots, core components, and embodied AI products. The center will advance standardization for robots used in specialized and emergency-response applications, while seeking to establish a national-level standardization platform in the Jinan Start-up Area. It will develop an integrated testing platform capable of handling heavy loads, explosion-proof requirements, strong electromagnetic interference, and extreme environmental conditions, with its testing capabilities covering a full range of products, from micro and small robots to large-scale robotic systems and low-altitude aircraft. It will primarily serve companies developing specialized robots for industries such as mining, petrochemicals, electric power, and metallurgy. With growing convergence of robotics and artificial intelligence (AI), the center will also develop capabilities for trustworthy AI evaluation, strengthening its capacity to test software security, information security, and AI models. It will focus on serving companies engaged in embodied AI, data services, and model training. The operation of the center is expected to reduce costs associated with R&D, testing, pilot-scale testing, and commercialization, while accelerating time to market. The Jinan Start-up Area has identified robotics and AI as priority industries for development during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). It has designated the robotics industry as a key driver for fostering new quality productive forces and is making full use of existing industrial facilities to build a comprehensive robotics ecosystem covering the entire industrial value chain. The area has already established several industrial platforms, such as the Shandong (Jinan) Embodied Intelligence Harbor. It is accelerating efforts to open up real-world application scenarios in automobile manufacturing, construction, medical care, elderly care, and emergency rescue. State Grid Changzhou Power Supply Company Delivers End-to-End Services to Accelerate Distributed PV Development
bd.description: CHANGZHOU, China, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On October 19, technicians from State Grid Changzhou Power Supply Company provided one-on-one consultations on the latest grid-connection policies and application procedures for distributed photovoltaic (PV) projects at Zhulin Town, Jintan District, Changzhou. Driven by fast-growing demand amid surging distributed PV interconnection capacity, the utility has moved its service frontline closer to customers. It cuts processing time with a "one-stop disclosure" policy and on-site assistance, delivering convenient support across the entire grid-connection chain. Take Jintan District as an example. The total installed capacity of grid-connected distributed PV projects in the region has exceeded 900 megawatts (MW) in 2026. Rapid capacity expansion has raised higher requirements for grid acceptance, operation and maintenance, and data management. The local power provider has coordinated efforts across pre-application, mid-process and post-commissioning stages to build a closed-loop service covering the full lifecycle of PV projects. At the pre-grid-connection stage, staff have carried out field inspections in rural areas including Xuebu Town. In strict compliance with national grid technical standards, they inspect PV modules, inverters, metering devices and earthing systems item by item, verify equipment parameters, and eliminate hidden risks in cable routing and protection device configuration. Technicians also answered on-site questions regarding interconnection procedures, power generation settlement and routine maintenance. They explained lightning and fire prevention measures as well as self-inspection guidelines in plain language, combining technical compliance checks with user guidance right at project sites. During the application process, the company strictly enforces the "one-time full disclosure" rule, clearly listing all procedures, required documentation and service timelines. It also offers tailored advice based on customers' actual power consumption scenarios to prevent repeated trips caused by incomplete paperwork or unclear procedures. At the post-commissioning operation and maintenance stage, to tackle low data collection rates for some PV assets, the team adopted manufacturer-specific solutions. They rolled out firmware upgrades, parameter tuning and communication module troubleshooting, restoring data collection and transmission links household by household and device by device. A dedicated issue log has been created to ensure full closed-loop follow-up and resolution of all faults. From initial consultation and site surveys to grid acceptance and post-launch follow-ups, State Grid Changzhou Power Supply Company provides proactive, end-to-end support throughout every phase of PV development. The company noted that it will continue to improve the full-process guarantee mechanism for new energy grid interconnection, carry out regular inspections and return visits for distributed PV systems, and steadily lift data collection integrity. Reliable grid services will underpin the region's green low-carbon transition and drive lean management of distributed PV operations.

ae.title: Xinhua Silk Road: National Robot Test and Assessment Center (Headquarters) establishes branch in Jinan Start-up Area
ae.description: BEIJING, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Yellow River Basin Center of the National Robot Test and Assessment Center (Headquarters) was officially inaugurated in Jinan Start-up Area for Growth Drivers Transformation in Shandong Province on October 16, addressing gaps in public services for the robotics industry across the region. The National Robot Test and Assessment Center is a nationally authorized testing and certification institution in China's robotics sector, serving as a key pillar of the country's robot testing and certification system. The newly-established Yellow River Basin Center, serving Shandong and the region across the Yellow River Basin, will establish an integrated platform that combines innovation and R&D, pilot-scale testing and smart manufacturing, data collection and training, data services, testing and certification, and industrial development for complete robots, core components, and embodied AI products. The center will advance standardization for robots used in specialized and emergency-response applications, while seeking to establish a national-level standardization platform in the Jinan Start-up Area. It will develop an integrated testing platform capable of handling heavy loads, explosion-proof requirements, strong electromagnetic interference, and extreme environmental conditions, with its testing capabilities covering a full range of products, from micro and small robots to large-scale robotic systems and low-altitude aircraft. It will primarily serve companies developing specialized robots for industries such as mining, petrochemicals, electric power, and metallurgy. With growing convergence of robotics and artificial intelligence (AI), the center will also develop capabilities for trustworthy AI evaluation, strengthening its capacity to test software security, information security, and AI models. It will focus on serving companies engaged in embodied AI, data services, and model training. The operation of the center is expected to reduce costs associated with R&D, testing, pilot-scale testing, and commercialization, while accelerating time to market. The Jinan Start-up Area has identified robotics and AI as priority industries for development during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). It has designated the robotics industry as a key driver for fostering new quality productive forces and is making full use of existing industrial facilities to build a comprehensive robotics ecosystem covering the entire industrial value chain. The area has already established several industrial platforms, such as the Shandong (Jinan) Embodied Intelligence Harbor. It is accelerating efforts to open up real-world application scenarios in automobile manufacturing, construction, medical care, elderly care, and emergency rescue. ae.title: State Grid Changzhou Power Supply Company Delivers End-to-End Services to Accelerate Distributed PV Development
ae.description: CHANGZHOU, China, Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On October 19, technicians from State Grid Changzhou Power Supply Company provided one-on-one consultations on the latest grid-connection policies and application procedures for distributed photovoltaic (PV) projects at Zhulin Town, Jintan District, Changzhou. Driven by fast-growing demand amid surging distributed PV interconnection capacity, the utility has moved its service frontline closer to customers. It cuts processing time with a "one-stop disclosure" policy and on-site assistance, delivering convenient support across the entire grid-connection chain. Take Jintan District as an example. The total installed capacity of grid-connected distributed PV projects in the region has exceeded 900 megawatts (MW) in 2026. Rapid capacity expansion has raised higher requirements for grid acceptance, operation and maintenance, and data management. The local power provider has coordinated efforts across pre-application, mid-process and post-commissioning stages to build a closed-loop service covering the full lifecycle of PV projects. At the pre-grid-connection stage, staff have carried out field inspections in rural areas including Xuebu Town. In strict compliance with national grid technical standards, they inspect PV modules, inverters, metering devices and earthing systems item by item, verify equipment parameters, and eliminate hidden risks in cable routing and protection device configuration. Technicians also answered on-site questions regarding interconnection procedures, power generation settlement and routine maintenance. They explained lightning and fire prevention measures as well as self-inspection guidelines in plain language, combining technical compliance checks with user guidance right at project sites. During the application process, the company strictly enforces the "one-time full disclosure" rule, clearly listing all procedures, required documentation and service timelines. It also offers tailored advice based on customers' actual power consumption scenarios to prevent repeated trips caused by incomplete paperwork or unclear procedures. At the post-commissioning operation and maintenance stage, to tackle low data collection rates for some PV assets, the team adopted manufacturer-specific solutions. They rolled out firmware upgrades, parameter tuning and communication module troubleshooting, restoring data collection and transmission links household by household and device by device. A dedicated issue log has been created to ensure full closed-loop follow-up and resolution of all faults. From initial consultation and site surveys to grid acceptance and post-launch follow-ups, State Grid Changzhou Power Supply Company provides proactive, end-to-end support throughout every phase of PV development. The company noted that it will continue to improve the full-process guarantee mechanism for new energy grid interconnection, carry out regular inspections and return visits for distributed PV systems, and steadily lift data collection integrity. Reliable grid services will underpin the region's green low-carbon transition and drive lean management of distributed PV operations.

za.title: 'Leave us alone!' DC golfers fear worst over Trump's course remodel
za.description: 'Leave us alone!' DC golfers fear worst over Trump's course remodel Estelle. Bronkhorst Wed, 10/21/2026 - 12:00 WASHINGTON - For years, Max Salas has enjoyed teeing off at Washington's East Potomac Golf Links, a public course nestled in the heart of the US capital where ordinary Americans can enjoy a round without breaking the bank. But President Donald Trump's controversial plans to remodel the course into a facility capable of hosting major championship- caliber events have left the 74-year-old retiree exasperated. "Leave us alone! Leave us alone!" Salas told AFP when asked what message he would send to Trump. "What the hell do we need a championship course in a public course?" he said. "We're here, we've been here for years, and it's ridiculous." Salas is among golfers worried that Trump's proposed overhaul of East Potomac could transform an affordable public amenity into an expensive destination beyond the reach of its regular players. At the moment, 18 holes at East Potomac costs a maximum of $48. That's a far cry from the kind of rates often found at privately owned golf courses -- such as those owned by Trump -- where green fees can often run into hundreds of dollars. Trump, a famously avid golfer, has claimed that East Potomac is not fit for purpose. AFP | SAUL LOEB "The current Course is old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect," Trump said on Sunday. "It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous, and disease-infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall." But for Salas, the remodel -- which will see the course closed from mid-November -- also raises questions about Trump's priorities at a time of international turmoil. "We're in the middle of a war, and he's over here trying to tinker with a golf course?" he said. "I mean, where is this guy's sense? Common sense?" - 'I cannot afford it' - The prospect of a championship-standard course might appeal to some golfers, but for others, the overriding concern is what the transformation could mean for their wallets. Fidel Enrique Garcia Rendon, a 59-year-old Pilates studio owner, fears the cost of playing the remodelled course will put it beyond his reach. "Unfortunately, if it goes to a championship course level, the fees are going to go from $22 to $250 or plus, $350 who knows?" he said. "So I definitely will not be able to come here and play because at that price, I cannot afford it." His concerns were echoed by fellow retiree Tom Carmody, who questioned both the eventual cost of the revamped course and whether the project would be completed. "It just makes me nervous, quite nervous," Carmody said. "For one, just his ability to follow through. I mean, what's going to happen? Will he stop halfway through or quit or something like that?" But Carmody's bigger concern is whether the promise of continued public access will mean much if green fees rise dramatically. "He talks about it remaining open to the public, but instead of $30 or $40 a round, maybe it's $120, $150 a round, which is going to eliminate a lot of people." AFP

tn.title: منتدى «إينوفيست 2026» يدقّ ناقوس الخطر بشأن تبذير الخبز في تونس ويدعو إلى تثمين النفايات
tn.description: في ظلّ التحديات الاقتصادية والبيئية الراهنة، تبرز ظاهرة تبذير الخبز وهدر الأغذية في تونس باعتبارها من الإشكاليات التي تستوجب مزيداً من الوعي والتحرّك المشترك، لما لها من انعكاسات مباشرة على الاقتصاد الوطني والموارد الطبيعية. وفي هذا الإطار، شكّل منتدى «إينوفيست 2026» (Inowaste 2026)، الذي نظمته اليوم الأربعاء 21 أكتوبر بالمنستير، الجمعية العلمية «المنستير المخبر الحي» برئاسة الأستاذ منير الزيلي، فضاءً للنقاش وتبادل الخبرات حول سبل توظيف الابتكار والاقتصاد الدائري للحدّ من هدر الغذاء وتحويل النفايات إلى موارد ذات قيمة اقتصادية وبيئية. سلّطت الدراسات العلمية المقدّمة خلال المنتدى، ولا سيما مداخلة الأستاذة هاجر دبابي ، الباحثة والمؤطّرة بالمعهد الوطني للعلوم الفلاحية بتونس، الضوء على حجم استهلاك الخبز في المجتمع التونسي وأبرز العوامل المؤدية إلى تبذيره، من بينها سوء تقدير الكميات المطلوبة وطرق الحفظ غير الملائمة. ووفق المعطيات التي عُرضت خلال الملتقى، يُقدّر معدّل استهلاك الفرد في تونس بنحو 74 كيلوغراماً من الخبز سنوياً، وهو ما يبرز أهمية ترشيد الاستهلاك والحدّ من الكميات التي ينتهي بها المطاف في النفايات. كما تناولت الدراسة الفارق بين سعر الخبز المدعّم الذي يدفعه المستهلك، والمقدّر بنحو 190 مليماً، وكلفته الحقيقية التي تبلغ، وفق الأرقام المقدّمة، حوالي 500 مليم، بما يعكس حجم مساهمة الدولة في دعم هذه المادة الأساسية. ويطرح هدر الخبز، في هذا السياق، إشكالاً اقتصادياً إضافياً، إذ تتحوّل الموارد المالية المخصّصة للدعم إلى خسائر كان بالإمكان الحدّ منها من خلال تحسين سلوك الاستهلاك وتعزيز الوعي بأهمية المحافظة على الغذاء. من جانبها، أكّدت الأستاذة حنان بن إسماعيل، الجامعية والمتخصّصة في الصناعات الغذائية بالمعهد الوطني للعلوم الفلاحية، أهمية اعتماد مقاربات مبتكرة تقوم على مفهوم «الحافز السلوكي» (Nudge)، بهدف تشجيع المستهلكين على تغيير عاداتهم اليومية والانتقال من سلوك التبذير إلى ثقافة ترشيد الاستهلاك. وأوضحت أن هدر الغذاء لا يقتصر على ضياع المواد الغذائية فحسب، بل يتسبّب أيضاً في هدر غير مباشر للموارد المستعملة في إنتاجها، على غرار المياه والطاقة، وهو ما يزيد من أهمية هذه المسألة في ظلّ التحديات المائية والطاقية التي تواجهها البلاد. كما استعرضت تجربة ميدانية أُنجزت بالشراكة مع جامعة بولونيا الإيطالية، ومنظمة الأمم المتحدة، ومركز «سيام باري»، تستهدف الشباب والطلبة، باعتبارهم فئة قادرة على المساهمة في ترسيخ سلوكيات استهلاك أكثر استدامة ونقلها إلى محيطهم العائلي والاجتماعي. ولم يقتصر المنتدى على تشخيص أسباب الهدر الغذائي، بل سعى إلى استكشاف حلول عملية تجمع بين البحث العلمي والابتكار والتطبيقات الاقتصادية. ومثّل اللقاء فرصة لتبادل التجارب بين الجامعيين والباحثين والطلبة وممثلي البلديات والشركات الناشئة، بهدف تطوير مبادرات قادرة على الحدّ من النفايات وتعزيز الاستغلال الأمثل للموارد. وشملت الحلول المطروحة توظيف تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي للمساعدة على التقليص من هدر الأغذية، إلى جانب تثمين المخلفات الفلاحية والنفايات العضوية عبر استخراج الزيوت وإنتاج مواد التجميل والأصباغ الطبيعية الصديقة للبيئة والموجّهة إلى قطاع النسيج. وتعكس هذه المقاربات توجّهاً نحو ترسيخ مبادئ الاقتصاد الدائري، الذي يقوم على تقليص النفايات وإعادة استخدامها وتثمينها، بما يفتح المجال أمام فرص اقتصادية جديدة ويدعم الابتكار والتنمية المستدامة. ويؤكّد منتدى «إينوفيست 2026» أن مواجهة تبذير الخبز والهدر الغذائي لا تقتصر على التوعية بأهمية المحافظة على الغذاء، بل تتطلّب أيضاً تغيير السلوكيات الاستهلاكية، وتطوير الحلول التكنولوجية، وتعزيز الشراكة بين البحث العلمي والمؤسسات الاقتصادية والمجتمع، من أجل تحويل النفايات من عبء بيئي واقتصادي إلى مورد قابل للتثمين والاستثمار. ابن حسن

tn.description: تعقد لجنة المالية والميزانية بمجلس نواب الشعب، اليوم جلسة تمهيدية تخصص للنظر في مشروع ميزانية الدولة لسنة 2027. وتأتي هذه الجلسة عقب إحالة الحكومة لمشروع قانون المالية وميزانية الدولة لسنة 2027 في الأجل الدستوري المحدد يوم 15 أكتوبر، لتبدأ اللجان المختصة بالبرلمان في دراسة التوازنات المالية الكبرى ورزنامة الاستماعات لأعضاء الحكومة. وتقدر وثيقة الميزانية مداخيل الدولة لسنة 2027 بنحو 54.28 مليار دينار، مقابل نفقات في حدود 68.895 مليار دينار. ويرتكز المشروع على خيارات استراتيجية تشمل مواصلة تكريس الدور الاجتماعي للدولة ومساندة صغار الفلاحين والمؤسسات الصغرى والناشئة والشركات الأهلية عبر خطوط تمويل تفاضلية. كما تتضمن التوجهات إقرار تدابير لتخفيف مديونية المنشآت والمؤسسات العمومية وتسهيل إجراءات السكن الاجتماعي إلى جانب تشجيع الانتقال الطاقي ودعم الاستثمار والنمو الاقتصادي. وينتظر أن تخصص هذه الجلسة لدراسة الفرضيات العامة التي بني عليها مشروع الميزانية (مثل سعر برميل النفط المتوقع ونسبة النمو المستهدفة وسعر صرف العملات) إلى جانب امكانية ضبط اللقاءات والاستماعات للوزراء وإطارات وزارة المالية.
